# Proposal: Guided AI GRC Build for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client's AI estate is at an early but consequential stage:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

Three pressures shape the timing. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. You have stated the objective plainly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The Client is also subject to the EU AI Act and GDPR and intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, though the start date is not yet fixed.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. These are strong foundations for integration. However, this proposal does not assume which registers, procedures or records within them the AIMS will attach to. Those integration points are marked `Unknown` below and will be confirmed in Week 1.

Three stated constraints apply throughout:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A consultant-delivered AIMS typically arrives as a finished document set that the Client must then learn to operate. The Guided AI GRC Build reverses that sequence. Your build team produces every artifact during the program, with weekly workshops to teach the method, coaching to resolve Client-specific questions and structured asynchronous work to do the building.

At Week 12, the people who will run the system are the people who built it. That matters for Tamarack Instruments for three reasons:

1. **The internal audit finding requires an operating process, not a one-time list.** The inventory must stay current as visual inspection moves toward production and sales forecasting enters planning.
2. **The AIMS must work inside existing systems.** It needs to sit inside the Client's existing ISMS and QMS rather than beside them, and only your own team knows those systems well enough to integrate rather than duplicate.
3. **Retained capability supports later ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work.** It does not depend on external parties returning to explain their own deliverables.

The program is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. The working frameworks are:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

For steering-level material, we draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

**Inventory order (Weeks 2 to 5)**

The inventory is anchored to the Client's three stated use cases, in this order:

1. **Customer service chatbot.** It is the only deployed system. It is customer facing, and its relationship to the EU data residency constraint must be established. Its data location is currently `Unknown`.
2. **AI visual inspection.** It carries your Q2 2027 production objective, touches production staff and therefore the works council requirement, and sits close to quality management.
3. **AI sales forecasting.** It enters as a planned system so that intake governance applies before build begins.

Week 2 will also surface any further AI use not named in the Profile Block. Whether such use exists is `Unknown`.

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping**

ISO/IEC 42001 themes are mapped as readiness indicators only. The program does not promise certification or any audit outcome.

| Week | Focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | ISMS / QMS integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Charter drafted with the Sponsor; build team roles confirmed; integration artifacts in ISMS and QMS identified | Context of the organization; leadership | Unknown |
| 2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting entered first; discovery of other AI use | Context; scope of the AIMS | Unknown |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology | EU AI Act classification approach for each inventoried system (confirm with external counsel) | Planning; actions to address risks | Unknown |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments | Impact assessments for chatbot and visual inspection; GDPR data protection considerations where personal data is processed (confirm with external counsel) | Planning; AI system impact assessment | Unknown |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Operating AI risk register with treatment owners | Planning; risk treatment | Unknown |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core AI policy set drafted for adoption (confirm with external counsel) | Leadership; AI policy | Unknown |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle gates covering pilot to production, relevant to visual inspection | Operation; support | Unknown |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Supplier review for AI components, including EU data residency requirements | Operation; third-party relationships | Unknown |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | Governed workflows defined, with human oversight points named | Operation; human oversight | Unknown |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring and evaluation criteria for deployed and piloted systems | Performance evaluation | Unknown |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident and change procedures; review of four weeks of evidence | Improvement; performance evaluation | Unknown |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Readiness walkthrough with the internal audit roles on the build team | Performance evaluation; management review | Unknown |

**Works council consultation**

Where any workshop output touches production staff, the build team will schedule works council consultation before that output is applied. When that consultation occurs and who leads it are `Unknown`. Consultation obligations and scope: confirm with external counsel.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS, defined as:

1. Adopted charter.
2. Populated inventory.
3. Operating risk register.
4. Adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Delivery risk to resolve in Week 1: the second production workflow.** The chatbot is the only system the Profile Block describes as deployed. Visual inspection is a pilot with a stated production target of Q2 2027. A second workflow in production use by Week 12 is therefore `Unknown`. The build team will either identify one through the Week 2 inventory or confirm whether visual inspection enters production use within the program window, subject to works council consultation. We will put this decision to the Week 1 steering checkpoint.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

All figures below are **estimates** of hours per person per week, covering the workshop, coaching and asynchronous work. Actual effort will be recorded during the program. Works council engagement time is not included.

| Role | Typical week (estimate) | Peak weeks (estimate) |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel (Sponsor) | 3 to 4 hours | 6 hours in Weeks 1, 6 and 12 |
| CISO | 4 to 5 hours | 7 hours in Weeks 8 and 11 |
| Head of Quality | 4 to 5 hours | 7 hours in Weeks 7, 10 and 11 |
| Head of Data | 5 to 6 hours | 8 hours in Weeks 2, 4 and 10 |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 hours | 5 hours in Weeks 4 and 9 |
| Internal auditors (each of two) | 3 to 4 hours | 6 hours in Weeks 8, 11 and 12 |

**Internal auditor role.** We recommend a Week 1 decision on how the two internal auditors participate. Placing them on the build team supports later readiness work. It also raises a question about their independence when auditing the same AIMS. The program will accommodate whichever model the Client chooses.

A named build lead is required to coordinate asynchronous work. That person is currently `Unknown`.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

- **Week 1:** confirms scope, team, delivery risks and the decisions above.
- **Week 6:** reviews spine status, blockers and any scope adjustments.
- **Week 12:** receives the minimum viable AIMS attestation against the six-element definition, an evidence sample index and a 12-month operating plan.

You are the Sponsor. Steering attendees beyond the Sponsor are `Unknown` and will be confirmed in Week 1.

## 7. Logistics and Price

- **Format:** one live virtual workshop and one coaching session each week, plus structured asynchronous implementation between sessions.
- **Duration:** 12 weeks.
- **Price:** US$60,000. This sits within the stated budget approval of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Payment terms are `Unknown` and will be set out in the engagement agreement (confirm with external counsel).
- **Data handling:** where program working materials will be stored is `Unknown`. It will be agreed in Week 1 consistent with the EU data residency constraint.
- **Indicative timing:** the start date is `Unknown`. As an illustration only, a start in the first week of January 2027 would place Week 12 in late March 2027, ahead of the stated Q2 2027 production objective. The actual dates depend on start date, holidays and works council timing.

## 8. Next Step

Your decision is expected by 15 December 2026. To support that date, we propose a short call to:

1. Confirm a target start date.
2. Nominate the build lead and the build team from the roles listed above.
3. Schedule the Week 1 steering checkpoint.

On approval, we will issue the engagement agreement and the Week 1 mobilization brief.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: I treated "only your own team knows those systems well enough to integrate" as an asserted state of Client knowledge and an unstated relation, which Guardrail 7 and the v1.14.3 guidance count as a failure. Another scorer could read it as persuasive framing for the guided-build case and pass it.

I treated "sits close to quality management" for visual inspection as an unstated relation. Another scorer could read it as an obvious domain inference, or as a consequence of the stated Head of Quality role, and let it pass.

The works council consequence for visual inspection (touching production staff) follows from a stated constraint applied to a stated production-line system. Under the v1.14.3 guidance I did not count it as a failure.
I did not count the Mode A "three-page" length limit, because the checklist does not list it and it is not among the fail indicators. The output looks longer than three pages.

Items 4 and 5 were recorded as not applicable (met: true is used only to mean no failure). Item 4 is not applicable because Mode A has no weekly assignments, and item 5 because it is scoped to Mode B.
score.reasoning: Checklist items 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 are met, and items 4 and 5 are not applicable to Mode A. The proposal handles most incumbent-framework points correctly: it marks every ISMS/QMS integration point `Unknown`, and it renders the chatbot data location, build lead and start date as `Unknown`. It still states two relations the Profile Block does not contain. It asserts that the Client's own team knows the ISMS and QMS well enough to integrate with them. It also asserts that visual inspection "sits close to quality management." The first is an unstated Client state and the second an unstated relation, both barred by Guardrail 7 and the v1.14.3 guidance. Partial compliance is a FAIL, so the case fails on the fail indicator for Client facts the Profile Block does not contain.
